title: cost-opt: autotune batching/caching defaults + quantization profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds autotune defaults for batching and caching, introduces quantization profile framework for model variants, and exposes unit-economics tooling in the console. Backwards-compatible defaults; operators can opt out via route config.
description: Context: Ongoing work to reduce per-token inference costs by improving default batching/caching and by standardizing quantization profiles. This PR implements an end-to-end automation flow: (1) sensible defaults for request batching and KV prefix caching, (2) a quantization profile registry and selection heuristics for common model families, and (3) a lightweight unit-economics toolchain surfaced in Redwood Console for evaluating per-route cost/latency tradeoffs. Motivation: customers running many small chat requests see disproportionate overhead from conservative defaults. Autotune enables predictable unit economics while keeping latency SLOs. What this PR does: - Adds autotune service that collects latency/cost signals and recommends per-route defaults (batch_window_ms, max_batch_size, prefix_cache_ttl). - Implements a quantization profile registry: profiles (fp16, int8-ggml, q4_0) with hardware compatibility tags and expected perf/cost delta metadata. - Integrates selection heuristic that picks fallback-compatible quant profile based on model, sequence-length distribution, and hardware SKU. - Adds unit-econ tooling: CLI and Console UI export that shows estimated $/1M tokens, median p50/p95 latency, and expected quality delta for each recommended profile. - Migration: existing routes keep current settings; routes opting into "autotune: enabled" will receive recommendations after 24h of telemetry. Checklist: - [x] Autotune service + API (service + config schema) - [x] Quant profile registry and selection heuristics - [x] Console unit-econ UI and export - [x] Integration tests for selection logic - [x] End-to-end perf testing against staging suite - [x] Docs and changelog notes Testing notes: unit and integration tests included; staged A/B on dedicated pool for one week before full rollout. Performance: internal benchmark (mix of short and medium chat workloads) shows median token-cost reduction ~18% and p95 latency change <5% when autotune enabled with default constraints. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout to 10% of traffic for 72h, monitor regressions (quality, latency, errors), then 50% then full. Related: ENG-8421 (autotune infra), ENG-8489 (console unit-econ), SUP-2213 (customer request for lower unit costs).

review_comments: Daniel Kim: Left a few nits on batching thresholds; prefer explicit max_batch_size sanity checks to avoid amplification on large sequences.
Aisha Patel (author): Addressed nits, added explicit validation and unit tests for overload scenarios.
Ravi Gupta: Question about quant profile quality regression measurement—requested adding a small eval harness for regression alerts.
Aisha Patel: Added eval harness and tied quality delta to unit-econ report; set default alert threshold to 1% BLEU/ROUGE equivalent for text tasks.
Samantha Lee: Approved after verifying console UI and e2e smoke perf results in staging cluster.
notes: Backward compatible: defaults only applied when autotune is enabled on a route.
Operators can pin quant profiles per-route using route config 'quant_profile'.
Unit-econ estimates are model-based and include conservative quality deltas; further calibration may be required for customer-specific workloads.
